Glossary

Web glossary: internet words explained simply

Domain name, hosting, SEO, HTTPS… You hear these words but don't know what they mean? Each page explains one word, with a real example.

BCEFGHILMPRSTW

B

BacklinkA link placed on another website that leads to yours: a kind of recommendation.Title tagThe blue title Google shows for each page of your website.

C

Call to actionThe button or phrase that invites visitors to act: call, book, order.CMSThe software that lets you change a website's pages without writing a line of code.

E

Professional emailAn address on your domain name, such as contact@votreboite.fr, instead of a free address.Extension (plugin)A small add-on you put on a website to give it one more feature.

F

robots.txt fileA small text file that tells search engine robots where they may go on your website.Contact formThe few boxes on your website that let a customer write to you without opening their email.

G

Google Search ConsoleGoogle's free tool for seeing how your website appears in its results.

H

Web hostingThe place where your website's files are stored so they can be seen day and night.HTTPS and SSL certificateThe little padlock in the address bar: your visitors exchange with you securely.

I

IndexingThe moment Google files a page in its catalogue, so it can show it later.

L

Landing pageA page built for a single offer and a single action, often tied to a campaign.Internal linkA link between two pages of your own website, to guide visitors and Google.

M

Website maintenanceThe regular upkeep that keeps a website safe, fast and working, month after month.Legal noticeThe required page that says who publishes the website, who hosts it and how to reach you.Meta descriptionThe two lines of summary shown under your page title in Google.KeywordThe words your customers type into Google, and that your website needs to use well.

P

Home pageThe first page of your website, which must say in a few seconds what you do.SitemapThe list of every page on your website, prepared so Google misses none of them.

R

Local SEOBeing found by people looking for your trade near them, in your town.SEO (natural search ranking)Everything that helps your website show up in Google's results without paying for ads.GDPR and cookiesThe European rules on personal data, and what they mean for your website.

S

Website backupA full copy of your website, kept safe, so everything can be put back after a problem.Web serverThe machine that receives visits to your website and sends the pages to each screen.Responsive websiteA website that adjusts itself to any screen: phone, tablet or computer.Visitor statisticsThe figures that show how many people visit your website, where they come from and what they look at.

T

Loading timeHow long a page takes to appear: a few seconds that matter a lot.ThemeThe design template that gives a website its colours, fonts and layout.

W

WordPressThe free software that runs a very large share of the world's websites.
